source_text:
Ἐν δὲ τούτοις οἱ μαθηταὶ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ῥαββί, φάγε. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγὼ βρῶσιν ἔχω φαγεῖν ἣν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε.

ἵνα δὲ τρανότερον νοηθῇ τὸ ῥητόν, σκεπτέον τίς ἡ βρῶσις αὕτη ἡ κρείττων τῆς τῶν μαθητῶν, ἣν οὐκ ᾔδεισαν.
pass_a_gloss: And in these things the disciples were asking him saying: Rabbi, eat. But he said to them: I have food to eat which you do not know. And in order that the said may be understood more clearly, one must examine what this food is that is better than that of the disciples, which they did not know.
pass_b_english: Meanwhile [[the disciples were asking him, “Rabbi, eat.” >> Bible:John 4:31]] But he said, [[“I have food to eat that you do not know.” >> Bible:John 4:32]]
To hear that clearly, we must ask what this food is — better than the disciples’ food, and unknown to them.
